abstract: Circular single-stranded DNA (CssDNA) offers unique advantages for molecular diagnostics and next-generation sequencing (NGS) due to its nuclease degradation resistance and compatibility with rolling circle amplification. CssDNA is used with several modern NGS platforms, but many library preparation workflows require a conversion step involving splinting and an enzymatic treatment, adding workflow complexity. This study introduces Nicking Loop™, a targeted library preparation method that converts single- and double-stranded DNA into CssDNA, enabling direct circular sequencing and controlled linear amplification that can be repeated over multiple generations. The method demonstrated improved preservation of variant allele frequencies across three amplification generations compared to PCR, which is particularly relevant for detection of low-abundance variants. Sequencing of Nicking Loop™ circular libraries on Pacific Biosciences Onso™ platform demonstrated direct compatibility without additional library conversion steps. Nicking Loop™ is compatible with consensus sequencing for Oxford Nanopore, highlighting its applicability across multiple NGS platforms. Furthermore, Nicking Loop™ introduces a loop-based indexing strategy that enables early sample indexing for parallel processing of multiple samples. This proof-of-concept demonstrates the feasibility of Nicking Loop™ library preparation across multiple NGS platforms, contributing to the growing adoption of circular NGS platforms for applications requiring sensitive and accurate detection of low-abundance targets.
